title: Rabbi Yishmael HaShuri
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 10:4 [Hyman’s locator is רה״ה] quotes the Mishnah as saying, “Rabbi Yishmael HaShuri and Rabbi Shimon say: They did not disagree,” and so on. Hyman calls this a scribal error and says it should read Rabbi Shimon Shuri, as in Mishnah Keritot 4:3. He points to Seder HaDorot’s reference to the beginning of Tosefta Terumot, chapter 5, and says his text there reads R’ Shimon Shuri.

notes.text: The supplied Hebrew has HaShuri/Shuri without zayin, while the catalog heading has HaShezuri. That letter difference remains a source question. The proposed first-name correction is Yishmael to Shimon; the text is not silently respelled.

The saved whole Venice Shabbat chapter 10 scalar at array [3][1] lies under halakhah 4 and reads Rabbi Yishmael HaShezuri and Rabbi Shimon. The saved whole Torat Emet Mishnah Keritot 4:3 reads Rabbi Shimon Shezuri and Rabbi Shimon. These attest Hyman's contrasting first-name readings and preserve the negation THEY DID NOT DISAGREE. Supplied רה״ה is left visible beside the named 10:4 match; its earlier conversion to beginning of halakhah 5 is not silently treated as a checked numbering scheme. HaShuri/Shuri without zayin remains Hyman's supplied form, distinct from catalog and named editions. Tosefta Terumot beginning 5 and Seder HaDorot remain Hyman's uninspected comparisons. The uninspected final title stays R'.

Hyman’s printed heading and quotation have HaShezuri, with a zayin, and the Shimon forms are Shezuri. The supplied text and its English spelling are retained. The Venice text of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 10:4 has Yishmael HaShezuri, while the Guggenheimer edition prints bracketed Shimon HaShezuri. Mishnah Keritot 4:3 has Shimon Shezuri. Seder HaDorot cites the beginning of chapter 5 of Tosefta Terumot and calls a scribal error possible. At 5:7 the consulted Hebrew text brackets the opening attribution to Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Shimon Shezuri, with Shezuri attached to Shimon.
